item.title: LVMH sales miss growth forecasts as China luxury demand slows
item.description: LVMH, the world's leading luxury group, said its sales edged higher in the third quarter despite a slowdown in demand in China hitting its fashion and leather goods segment.

item.title: Benjamin Netanyahu orders prosecution of 'NAZA' documentary interviewees
item.description: Netanyahu has called for a criminal investigation into soldiers and officers interviewed in award-winning documentary.

item.title: Child marriage in southern Germany: Over 350 cases recorded, some brides as young as 11
item.description: A written question by two AfD members of the Baden-Württemberg state parliament revealed 358 marriages involving minors, but only eight have so far been annulled with final legal effect.

item.title: Pakistan: Passenger train derailment kills at least five, injures more than 30
item.description: At least five people were killed and more than 30 injured when the Rehman Baba Express derailed near Multan, Pakistan, early on Tuesday, 13 October. An investigation has been launched into the cause of the accident.

item.title: Euronews tops rankings as fastest growing English-language news website
item.description: Euronews is the fastest-growing news website in the English-speaking world for the second month in a row, nearly doubling its audience as rivals shed readers.

item.title: EU sovereignty is ‘a need’ in the space, Sateliot CEO says
item.description: Jaume Sanpera, CEO of Spanish satellite operator Sateliot, believes Europe needs to “wake up” and avoid becoming dependent on two global power blocs. The industry, he argues, needs “a push” to help European tech companies become global champions.

item.title: Ceuta awaits King Felipe after summer migration crisis
item.description: Ceuta braces for a symbolic royal visit by King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia after a mass migration crisis strained the enclave’s social cohesion.

item.title: Fuel prices: Sébastien Lecornu promises €10 cut per fill-up
item.description: In France, pump prices are among the highest in the European Union. The government has moved to cut the price per litre by 12 to 18 centimes, the Prime Minister said on Monday.

item.title: German nationals among those airlifted to safety as storms kill five in Mexico
item.description: Heavy rain and strong winds have caused serious damage in Baja California and Guerrero, where authorities seek six missing and deploy thousands of rescue workers amid further flood risk.

item.title: Lufthansa Group boosts Japan network with up to 50 flights per week from summer 2027
item.description: Due to a ‘strong increase in demand’, the group’s airlines will offer up to 50 weekly flights to four Japanese airports next summer.

item.title: Could the European Security Council be the EU’s answer to hybrid attacks?
item.description: The European Commission proposed a new European Security Council (ESC) to respond to a recent surge in state-sponsored hybrid warfare, like cyberattacks and sabotage.

item.title: No respite for Ukraine despite Trump’s energy truce announcement
item.description: Good morning from Brussels. It’s Tuesday, and I’m Mared Gwyn. In today’s newsletter: Russia hits Ukraine’s energy sites despite Trump’s truce announcement, Europe stands firm behind Kyiv and France braces for fresh protests.

item.title: US actress Selma Blair accused of attacking cabin crew members on flight to New York
item.description: US media said that Blair punched one flight attendant and bit another. The 54-year-old then reportedly assaulted a police officer and nurse as she was transported to hospital.

item.title: More parks, rivers and green corridors: how Guimarães is preparing for extreme heat
item.description: Guimarães, the current European Green Capital, is reshaping the city to tackle extreme heat and climate change. Over a decade of investment in green corridors and river restoration has already lowered temperatures in some urban areas.

item.title: Europe Today: NATO warns Russia amid escalating hybrid attacks from Moscow
item.description: NATO's top commander has a message for Moscow: any attack on the alliance will be blocked, blunted and broken. In Warsaw, Zelenskyy says Russia has already broken Trump's energy ceasefire. And in France, student protests enter a new phase as the country's budget reaches the French Assembly.

item.title: US theme park operator Six Flags shuts nine roller coasters after man dies
item.description: Police are investigating after TV footage showed riders being evacuated from the 60-metre high Goliath ride.

item.title: Belgium: 9 minors arrested as clashes erupt near Brussels-Midi
item.description: Clashes near Brussels-Midi station leave around ten arrested, including nine minors, as student and anti-austerity protests continue in Belgium.

item.title: 'People survive on one meal a day': Oleshky official warns against giving Russia more territory
item.description: In a rare glimpse into life under Russian occupation, Tetiana Hasanenko, head of the Oleshky city military administration, told Euronews of spreading hunger and residents risking their lives to find food on the "road of death."

item.title: Bulgaria to summon Russian ambassador after ships hit in Black Sea, PM Radev says
item.description: Similar incidents have renewed scrutiny of Europe's ability to protect shipping and critical infrastructure in the Black Sea, more than a year after the EU launched a strategy to strengthen security in the region.

item.title: ‘We’re not waiting anymore’: Media mogul Mo Abudu opens a new hub for African cinema in London
item.description: Nigerian media mogul Mo Abudu has opened EbonyLife Place London, a new cultural hub celebrating African cinema and Black culture. The venue brings together a cinema, restaurant and boutique showcasing designers from Africa and its diaspora.

item.title: RJ Mitte, 'Breaking Bad' actor and disability rights champion, dies at age 34
item.description: Mitte played Walter White Jr., the son of Bryan Cranston’s chemistry teacher-turned-meth dealer Walter White on nearly every episode of the five seasons of the AMC show.

item.title: ‘Outdated and inadequate’: Tefal manufacturer urged to drop ‘forever chemicals’ from non-stick pans
item.description: The legal notice came from three environmental groups in the midst of fierce discussions over upcoming EU PFAS legislation, expected in 2027.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 13th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 13th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Glass igloos, sky villas and boutique suites: New places to stay in Finnish Lapland this winter
item.description: Finnish Lapland is a winter wonderland with plenty of things to see and do as well as a variety of places to stay. Here we take a look at some of the new accommodation options.

item.title: Rent surges in Georgia and Armenia as Russians flee fearing mobilisation
item.description: Monthly rents in Yerevan now run to €800–900 for a two-room flat, up 23.5% year on year in August, while Tbilisi rents have stabilised after 60–70% jumps following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Russian nationals account for 72% of all foreign property transactions in Armenia.

item.title: Can AI help healthcare move from treatment to prevention?
item.description: AI could help identify people at risk of developing certain conditions before they become ill, allowing healthcare providers to intervene earlier. But technology alone will not deliver that change.

item.title: This French AI stock is up 570% in 2026: Analysts see a further 90% upside
item.description: Despite its extraordinary rally, Bank of America analysts have upgraded Soitec SA stock to Buy and see potential for a further 90% upside.

item.title: Trump insists Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' is in place, drone strike kills woman in Kyiv
item.description: Trump insisted an energy ceasefire was in place between Russia and Ukraine despite reported Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy sites. A Russian drone hit a Kyiv apartment block, killing one woman and injuring at least five.

item.title: IMF forecasts 3.1% global growth in 2026, with eurozone at 1.1%
item.description: The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1%, citing resilient economies and AI investment. However, high energy prices linked to conflicts will weigh on growth, with eurozone expansion forecast at 1.1%.

item.title: Ceuta troops absent as Spain holds National Day parade in Madrid
item.description: The parade took place against a tense political backdrop, after Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called a snap general election for 29 November.

item.title: Portugal begins construction of high-speed rail line linking Lisbon and Porto
item.description: “Alongside the new Lisbon airport, high-speed rail lines represent the largest infrastructure projects the country will undertake this century," Miguel Pinto Luz, Portugal's minister of infrastructure and housing, said.

item.title: French navy intercepts and boards 'shadow fleet' ship, Macron says
item.description: Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence says the DF Peak tanker is involved in the transportation of Russian crude oil and that it is associated with the Sovcomflot shipping firm.

item.title: Citroën's iconic 2CV returns as an all-electric model
item.description: Nearly 40 years after production ended, the iconic 2CV returns at the Paris Motor Show as a fully electric city car, keeping things simple and affordable in an increasingly competitive market.

item.title: French investigators use DNA and vehicle tracking to solve stolen Renoirs case
item.description: The arrests were prompted by the "very strong suspicion that another heist was imminent," the Marseille prosecutor said.

item.title: Spain: National Day highlights territorial unity from Barcelona to Ceuta
item.description: Spain's National Day on Monday, 12 October, was marked by demonstrations in Barcelona in support of Spanish unity, while far-right leader Santiago Abascal visited Ceuta, the Spanish enclave on the North African coast.

item.title: Blindsided again by Trump, Europe puts on a brave face and rallies behind Ukraine
item.description: European leaders closed ranks and rallied behind Ukraine as news of the diesel deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin continued to send shockwaves across the alliance.

item.title: EU struggles to ramp up Red Sea mission as Houthis escalate attacks
item.description: The EU and Italy are pushing member states to bolster the Aspides naval mission in the Red Sea, but only two more warships have been pledged, exposing Europe’s thin defence capabilities as the Houthis threaten energy supply routes.

item.title: UK PM Burnham says 'status quo' with Brussels 'not good enough' as he details upcoming EU summit
item.description: Burnham has repeatedly signalled his intention to move the UK closer to the EU since taking office in July and recently said reentering the bloc was one of a number of options for the country moving forward.

item.title: EU-China trade deal raises fears Brussels will go soft on Beijing
item.description: The EU's new trade deal with China has eased fears of an escalating trade war, but it could also weaken the political momentum behind Brussels' plans to take a tougher stance against Beijing's economic practices.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 12th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 12th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: EU agrees new security mission in Lebanon as UN peacekeepers prepare to leave
item.description: EU foreign ministers approved a civilian-military mission to train Lebanon’s armed forces. It will not replace UNIFIL, whose mandate ends in December. Personnel numbers and participating countries are yet to be confirmed.

item.title: NATO commander unveils strategy to make any attack on alliance ‘utterly futile’
item.description: Alexus Grynkewich says the new strategy aims to deny adversaries a foothold and dismantle their warfighting capabilities, telling the Warsaw Security Forum that NATO is prepared to block, blunt and break any attack.

item.title: 44-year-old woman rescued after 20 hours in sea, Greek coastguard says
item.description: The woman, from El Salvador, was found by the cargo ship MSC Rossella III, which was taking part in search efforts, the coastguard said in a statement.

item.title: Nuclear war and malicious use of AI could end humanity by 2100, scientists warn
item.description: They are among 17 global threats to human health according to a new study by The Lancet which aims to drive global action to address them.

item.title: Greece's social media ban for under-15s: What you need to know
item.description: The government argues that setting a clear age limit, combined with reliable age checks, will help protect children from potential risks associated with social media usage.

item.title: Hundreds of French supermarkets hit by cyberattack on refrigeration systems
item.description: Several supermarkets were forced to discard fresh and frozen food, Intermarché said, and have yet to estimate the losses. The Paris prosecutor has opened an investigation.

item.title: Paris’s oldest covered food market gutted by major overnight fire
item.description: Fire tore through Paris’s oldest covered food market in the Marais, leaving traders devastated. An investigation is under way and the market may stay shut for months.

item.title: Hard-right Reform party pledges to suspend UK asylum system for up to five years if elected
item.description: Reform has accused Labour of having "totally lost control" of the UK's borders, whilst Labour says small boat crossing figures have continued to come down in recent years.

item.title: Spreading the flow: cruise tourism helps Europe protect local identity
item.description: Europe’s tourism strategy is shifting to sustainable, year-round travel, promoting lesser-known destinations, local culture and smarter visitor management.

item.title: Explore the patterns of Qatar’s visual identity and architectural language
item.description: Cult explores the visual language of Qatar, where geometry isn’t ornamental. At the Doha Design District, we learn about 15 patterns from the Msheireb Pattern Collection, tracing their cultural and architectural origins, revealing how design can carry memory, identity and a sense of belonging.
